prompt.context: Our client is a manufacturing firm headquartered in Boston with manufacturing centers around the US. It has seen profits declining and is looking at ways to improve profitability. The firm has identified one area of interest that they wish us to advise them on: they currently lease a private jet to take executives to and from meetings in different cities. The lease is set to expire next week.
prompt.question: What should we do regarding the expiring private jet lease?

clarifying_info.q: What does the current lease cost?
clarifying_info.a: The lease is the only fixed cost and represents 75% of total annual costs. Total annual costs are approximately $2,000K. Other variable cost components include fuel/maintenance and crew. (See Exhibit 1 for cost breakdown.)

clarifying_info.q: How is the jet being utilized — which cities and how many trips?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 2 for utilization data. Cities served include Philadelphia (100 trips, 210 miles one way), New York (50 trips, 210 miles one way), and Cleveland (50 trips, 650 miles one way).

clarifying_info.q: How much does a round-trip first-class commercial ticket cost?
How many executives typically travel on each flight?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 2 passenger distribution chart. Roughly 20% of flights carry 1-3 passengers, 60% carry 4-6 passengers, and 20% carry 7+ passengers. The overall average is approximately 5 passengers per flight.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other types of jets we could lease instead?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. Three jet types are available: Type 1 (current) — max seats 15, max distance 2,000 miles, lease cost $1,500K; Type 2 — max seats 15, max distance 1,000 miles, lease cost $1,000K; Type 3 — max seats 8, max distance 1,000 miles, lease cost $500K.

clarifying_info.q: Is the ratio of fixed to variable costs the same across jet types?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the ratio of fixed (lease) to variable costs is similar across all aircraft types (lease = 75% of total cost).

exhibits.title: Annual Costs of Leased Jet
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the annual cost breakdown of the current leased jet, totaling approximately $2,000K

exhibits.title: Utilization Data and Passenger Distribution
exhibits.shows: Two panels: (1) a table of destinations showing number of trips and one-way distance; (2) a stacked bar chart showing the distribution of passengers per flight across all routes

framework: Understand the current lease cost structure (fixed vs. variable, total annual spend)
Map utilization: destinations, trip frequency, distances, and passenger counts
Enumerate and evaluate alternatives: (a) renew current lease, (b) lease a smaller/cheaper jet, (c) switch to commercial flights, (d) buy a plane, (e) use trains/videoconferencing
Quantify the cost of each viable alternative and compare to status quo
Assess qualitative factors: flexibility, privacy, executive time, confidentiality
Recommend the least-cost option that meets operational requirements

questions.prompt: What are the total annual costs of the current lease arrangement, and what is the cost breakdown?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about lease cost AND prompt for additional variable costs (fuel, maintenance, crew). Strong answer recognizes that the lease is the only fixed cost at 75% of total, implying variable costs = 25%. Total annual cost ~$2,000K; lease cost ~$1,500K.

math.setup: Total annual cost = $2,000K. Lease (fixed) = 75% x $2,000K. Variable costs = 25% x $2,000K.
math.answer: Annual lease = $1,500K; annual variable costs = $500K; total = $2,000K

questions.prompt: What would it cost to fly all executives on commercial first-class flights instead of the private jet?
questions.guidance: Candidate must remember to multiply ticket price by number of passengers (not just trips). Using ~5 passengers per flight as the average, compute total commercial cost for each city and sum. Strong candidates note this replaces only variable costs (since the private jet is gone) and compare total commercial spend to total current cost.

math.setup: Average passengers = 5 per flight (from Exhibit 2 distribution). Round-trip first-class fares: Philadelphia $300, New York $600, Cleveland $1,400. Commercial cost = trips x passengers x fare.
steps: New York: 50 trips x 5 passengers x $600 = $150,000 = $150K
math.answer: Total annual commercial flight cost ≈ $650K vs. current $2,000K — savings of ~$1,350K per year

questions.prompt: What would it cost to lease a different type of jet (Type 2 or Type 3), and which types are viable?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first check max distance against actual routes. Farthest destination is Cleveland at 650 miles one way. Type 2 (max 1,000 miles) covers all routes; Type 3 (max 1,000 miles) also covers distance but max 8 seats — given average of 5 passengers and some flights with 7+, Type 3 is likely too small. Type 1 vs. Type 2: lease cost drops from $1,500K to $1,000K. Total cost for Type 2 must account for variable costs using same 75/25 ratio.

math.setup: For Type 2: lease = $1,000K = 75% of total cost. Total cost = lease / 0.75.
steps: Type 3 ruled out: max 8 seats insufficient for flights with 7+ passengers (~20% of flights)
math.answer: Type 2 jet total annual cost ≈ $1,333K (savings of ~$667K vs. current). Type 3 is not viable due to seat capacity constraints.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the alternatives to renewing the existing private jet lease?

categories.name: Renew or upgrade lease
ideas: Lease a smaller, lower-cost jet (Type 2) that still meets range and capacity needs
Negotiate a multi-year lease discount on any jet type

categories.name: Switch to commercial aviation
ideas: Commercial first-class flights for all executive travel
Corporate travel management program for discounted fares
Mix: commercial for short/cheap routes, private for long/confidential trips

categories.name: Ground transportation alternatives
ideas: Train (Amtrak) for short-haul routes like Philadelphia and New York
Chartered bus for group travel on nearby routes

categories.name: Eliminate or reduce travel
ideas: Hybrid model: video for routine check-ins, in-person only for critical meetings

categories.name: Asset ownership
ideas: Purchase a plane outright (high capex, depreciation, long-term commitment)
Fractional jet ownership (e.g., NetJets) for flexibility without full lease

recommendation: Do not renew the private jet lease. Switch to commercial first-class flights for all executive travel.
Commercial flights cost approximately $650K per year vs. $2,000K for the current arrangement — annual savings of ~$1,350K with no compromise on reaching any destination currently served.
risks: Loss of privacy: executives may have confidential discussions on commercial flights
Loss of scheduling flexibility: dependent on airline schedules and availability
Potential productivity loss from longer travel times (connections, check-in, delays)
Executive dissatisfaction if they value the convenience of private aviation
next_steps: Negotiate a corporate travel account with preferred airlines for first-class discounts
Evaluate whether videoconferencing can replace a portion of lower-priority trips to further reduce costs
Consider fractional jet ownership as a middle-ground option if confidentiality or flexibility is deemed critical after stakeholder review
Re-examine multi-year lease discount options for Type 2 jet as a fallback if commercial is rejected
